newsitem.title: CHINA: Britain "less than gracious" before leaving HK-NZ.
newsitem.headline: Britain "less than gracious" before leaving HK-NZ.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters accused Britain on Wednesday of being "less than gracious" just before Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule

"If you're going to go to all this trouble and all the negotiations (over Hong Kong's handover) to bring it to finality, why in the last few hours of a long relationship just ruin it by being less than gracious?" Peters told reporters after meeting the territory's new leader Tung Chee-hwa.
Britain criticised China's plan to dispatch over 4,000 troops to the territory in the hours surrounding the midnight handover on Monday, ending 156 years of colonial rule.

Peters said he thought Beijing and the people of Hong Kong appreciated New Zealand taking an independent stance, referring to a decision to attend the swearing-in of a Beijing-appointed legislature in the early hours of July 1.
That ceremony was shunned by British and American leaders, though they sent diplomats.
China has scrapped Hong Kong's elected legislature and replaced it with an appointed chamber which operates until a new legislature is formed through an election to be held next May.
Peters added New Zealand had a constructive relationship with Hong Kong and had cooperated with it on trade issues such as cutting tariffs.
